title: Madras HC Quashes a Three-Year Debarment Over a Tender Clause Reading
case_name: Eco Protection Engineers Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Tamil Nadu
citation: 2026 LiveLaw (Mad) 464; W.P. No. 16595 of 2026, decided 5 August 2026
card_summary: Chennai's water board declared Eco Protection Engineers' joint-venture tender bid non-responsive, then debarred the firm and its partner from Board and ADB-financed contracts for three years, treating the disputed eligibility conditions as fraud. Justice Mohammed Shaffiq quashed the debarment, holding a genuine dispute over how a tender clause should be read cannot, by itself, amount to fraud.
card_tip: A procuring authority needs actual evidence of a fraudulent practice before debarring a bidder; a disagreement over how a tender clause reads is not enough to support blacklisting.
verification_notes: Parties, the CMWSSB Ring Main System tender, the 16 April 2026 debarment order, the three-year ADB and Board-wide bar, and the 5 August 2026 quashing on the ground that a clause-interpretation dispute is not fraud are consistent across LiveLaw, PrimeLegal and the order copy hosted by Verdictum. Reported as 2026 LiveLaw (Mad) 464.
